subject: Re: Post-scan consent / grace-window + HubSpot sync for DevCon kiosk
messages:
From: SmartScan Ops <ops@smartscan.io>

Cc: Samantha Lewis <samantha@devcon.org>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DevCon kiosk — post-scan opt-in / grace-window approach

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from the hardware side as we finalize firmware for your rented badge scanners: we've had multiple requests to support a 'post-scan consent grace window' — i.e., when an attendee scans, we capture the minimal lead record (badge_id, timestamp), then present a short on-screen prompt where they can opt in to marketing within 24–72 hours via SMS/email link. If they opt in later, we retroactively attach consent to the existing lead rather than create duplicate contacts.

Questions for your team:
- Is Redwood OK with us writing to your HubSpot endpoint to update an existing contact after the fact (PATCH by badge_id / email)?
- If the scanner is offline and we batch uploads, what dedupe key do you prefer (badge_id vs. email vs. external_id)?
- Any mandatory consent wording or fields you need captured so you can satisfy audit evidence?

We're attaching a short PDF describing offline handshakes and the minimal payload. Hoping to avoid a last-minute change at badge pickup.

Thanks,
Marko (SmartScan)
Ops, SmartScan Inc.
attachments: scanner-offline-handshake.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DevCon kiosk — post-scan opt-in / grace-window approach

Marko — thanks for the heads up and for the PDF. High level we can support the flow but need to lock two things before you ship firmware:

1) Dedupe key: use badge_id as the primary dedupe key for initial ingest. If the attendee later provides an email during the grace window we will merge by badge_id -> email. Do not create a new contact if badge_id is present.

2) Consent fields: please capture the full consent timestamp, consent_channel (kiosk), consent_text_version (v2) and consent_source_id (scanner_serial). I attached our recommended consent snippet for the screen copy (consent_snippet_v2.docx). That wording maps to our audit evidence.

3) Offline batch behavior: we accept newline-delimited JSON bundles over SFTP or the HubSpot batch API. If you batch, include a final manifest with checksums and the earliest_scan_ts for each record.

Cc'ing Ben (field ops) and Laura (CRM) to confirm mapping and ingestion expectations.

Action items: Ben to confirm handshake and retry/backoff; Laura to confirm HubSpot field map. We'll aim to finalize by COB Monday so firmware can be QA'd.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: DevCon kiosk — post-scan opt-in / grace-window approach

Thanks Marissa / Marko. A few tech notes from Field Ops:  

- Scanner modes: online mode = immediate POST to our ingestion endpoint; offline mode = local queue + batch upload every 10 min or on network restore. In offline mode include badge_id + device_serial + local_seq so we can detect replays.
- Dedupe: badge_id is fine. If an email arrives later in the grace window we will upsert contact by badge_id and set email field (HubSpot supports a merge). Please make sure your scan UX does not generate transient placeholder emails.
- Payload: we expect fields: badge_id, timestamp_utc, scanner_serial, scan_location_id, consent_flag (true/false), consent_text_version, consent_ts (ISO8601), optin_channel (kiosk|sms|email). Sample payload attached (ndjson in scanner-offline-handshake.pdf).
- Rate limiting: we allow bursts for events but please implement exponential backoff; include a device_id header for tracing.

Also note: privacy/regulatory constraint — if the attendee explicitly declines consent, do not send any PII to HubSpot. Only send anonymized badge_id with decline_reason.

I'll sync with Laura on the HubSpot field map.

Ben Carter
Field Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DevCon kiosk — post-scan opt-in / grace-window approach

All — looping in CRM mapping details. A few clarifications so our ingestion pipeline writes to the correct HubSpot properties without creating duplicates:  

- Primary external_id = badge_id (custom property: external_badge_id). HubSpot dedupe must be disabled for email during the initial ingest to avoid collision with pre-existing contacts — we'll control merges server-side.
- Map consent_text_version -> property: marketing_consent_version (string). Map consent_ts -> marketing_consent_at (datetime). Map consent_channel -> marketing_consent_channel (enum: kiosk,sms,email).
- Required boolean property: marketing_opted_in (true|false). If false, do not populate email/phone in the same payload.

I'm attaching a CSV with the canonical field map (hubspot-field-map.csv). Marko: when you do the retrospective opt-in link, please POST to the update endpoint with the external_badge_id and a consent payload. We will set the contact as opted-in and merge any email provided.

One more ask: please include a HubSpot event id in the payload so we can attribute lead source properly (property: first_touch_event).

If we can get a sample ndjson and a redacted batch file before Monday we can run a dry ingest in our staging HubSpot.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
CRM & Data Ops, Redwood Inference

Quick summary and next steps so we're all aligned:  

Decisions:
- Use badge_id as primary dedupe key for initial ingest; retrospective opt-ins will PATCH by badge_id and merge email if present.
- Consent fields required: consent_ts, consent_channel, consent_text_version, scanner_serial; marketing_opted_in boolean enforced.
- If attendee declines, send only anonymized badge_id with decline flag; do not transmit PII.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- SmartScan (Marko): provide a sample offline ndjson batch and an example of a retrospective opt-in POST by EOD Monday (Sep 6). Include device_id and local_seq fields.
- Ben: validate retry/backoff and confirm SFTP manifest format by Sep 3.
- Laura: run a dry ingest in staging once sample is provided; confirm no duplicate creation by Sep 8.
- Marissa: finalize on-screen consent copy (attached) and confirm with DevCon legal.

Thanks everyone — this approach keeps the badge pickup UX fast and gives attendees a clear path to opt in later while preserving auditability.
